questions.q: An embryologist removes the notochord from an experimental embryo, and the overlying ectoderm fails to thicken into a neural plate. Which structure normally induces the neural plate?

options.e: Wrong. It segments into somitomeres and somites; it is not the inducer of the neural plate.
Correct. The notochord induces the overlying ectoderm to become taller and form the neural plate.
Wrong. The crest is a product of the neural folds, formed after the plate; it cannot induce it.
Wrong. It forms the paired urogenital organs.

questions.q: A newborn has lumbosacral spina bifida with myelomeningocele. His mother took valproate during early pregnancy. Which structure failed to close, and on which day does it normally close?

options.e: Wrong pair. Failure of the cranial (anterior) neuropore, which closes on day 25, causes anencephaly.
Wrong day. The caudal neuropore closes on day 28, not 25.
Wrong pair. The cranial neuropore closes earlier, on day 25.
Correct. A lumbosacral defect means the posterior (caudal) neuropore, which closes on day 28.

questions.q: A woman takes a known teratogen in the 5th week of pregnancy. During which period is the embryo most susceptible to major structural malformations?

options.e: Wrong. The most sensitive period for major malformations is the 3rd to 8th week, when organs form.
Correct. The embryonic period (organogenesis) is the critical period for major malformations.
Wrong. The window is the 3rd to 8th week, not 4th to 10th.
Wrong. Organogenesis ends with the embryonic period at the end of week 8.

questions.q: A 2-year-old child has severe chronic constipation and a megacolon. Biopsy shows absence of ganglion cells in the distal colon. These ganglion cells normally arise from which embryonic cell population?

options.e: Correct. Autonomic (including enteric) ganglia are neural crest derivatives; Hirschsprung disease is failed crest migration.
Wrong. The neural tube forms the CNS (brain and spinal cord), not peripheral ganglia.
Wrong. It forms smooth muscle and serosa of the gut wall, not the ganglion cells.
Wrong. Endoderm forms the epithelial lining of the gut.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man has episodic headache, sweating and paroxysmal hypertension. Imaging shows a pheochromocytoma. Which row correctly gives the part of the suprarenal gland and its embryonic origin?

options.e: Wrong. Intermediate mesoderm gives the suprarenal cortex (per lecture), not the medulla.
Wrong. The cortex is mesodermal; only the medulla is a crest derivative.
Correct. Chromaffin cells of the suprarenal medulla come from the neural crest.
Wrong. Surface ectoderm forms epidermis and related structures, not the adrenal.

questions.q: A newborn is cyanotic and echocardiography shows a single arterial trunk (persistent truncus arteriosus) due to failure of the conotruncal septum to form. Which cells contribute to this septum?

options.e: Wrong. They form somites (vertebrae, skeletal muscle, dermis).
Wrong. Endoderm forms epithelial linings and gland parenchyma.
Correct. The conotruncal septum of the heart is a neural crest derivative.
Wrong. They form the urogenital organs.

questions.q: Which of the following meningeal layers is derived from neural crest spongioblasts?

options.e: Wrong. The dura is mesodermal, not a crest derivative.
Wrong. Arachnoid is a crest derivative but the dura is not.
Wrong. Pia is a crest derivative but the dura is not.
Correct. The leptomeninges (pia and arachnoid) come from the neural crest.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman has a midline neck mass that moves with swallowing. Which of the following glands has a parenchyma of endodermal origin?

options.e: Wrong. It is ectodermal.
Correct. Thyroid, parathyroid, liver, pancreas, thymus and tonsils have endodermal parenchyma.
Wrong. It is ectodermal (the anterior lobe arises from oral ectoderm).
Wrong. It is ectodermal, like other skin appendages.

questions.q: A patient with chronic otitis media has infection of the tympanic cavity and Eustachian tube. The epithelium lining these structures arises from which germ layer?

options.e: Wrong. Surface ectoderm forms the external auditory meatus and outer layer of the tympanic membrane, not the cavity.
Wrong. It forms ganglia, Schwann cells and some skull bones, not the lining epithelium.
Correct. The tympanic cavity and Eustachian tube are endodermal.
Wrong. It forms bone, muscle and dermis, not an epithelial lining.

questions.q: An embryo is examined on day 20 of development. Where does the first pair of somites appear?

options.e: Wrong. The first pair appears in the occipital region.
Wrong. Somites form cranio-caudally starting occipitally.
Wrong. The first pair is occipital.
Correct. Somites start in the occipital region at about day 20 and form craniocaudally (7 somitomeres lie in the head).

questions.q: An aborted embryo in the 4th week of development is examined. Which parameter best estimates its age?

options.e: Correct. The 1st month is the somite period (3 somites appear daily from day 20 to 30).
Wrong. CR length is used later; in week 4 somite count is the best estimate.
Wrong. Not used for the 4th week embryo.
Wrong. Not the best estimate for age in the 4th week.

questions.q: An infant has multiple hemivertebrae. Defective differentiation of which part of the somite is the cause?

options.e: Wrong. It forms the dermis of the skin.
Correct. The ventromedial part of the somite, the sclerotome, forms the vertebral column.
Wrong. It forms striated (skeletal) muscle.
Wrong. It is the dorsolateral part that gives the dermatome and myotome, not vertebrae.

questions.q: A fetus has bilateral renal agenesis and absent gonads. Defective development of which part of the intraembryonic mesoderm is the most likely cause?

options.e: Wrong. It forms somites and their derivatives.
Wrong. It forms body wall muscles and parietal serous membranes.
Correct. It gives the paired urogenital organs: gonads, genital ducts, kidneys and ureters.
Wrong. It forms cardiac and visceral smooth muscle.

questions.q: A child has a defect in the muscular wall of the gut and in the visceral serous membrane covering it. Which embryonic tissue is responsible?

options.t: Somatic (parietal) layer of lateral plate mesoderm
options.e: Wrong. It forms abdominal and thoracic wall muscles and parietal serous layers.
Wrong. It forms somites (bone, skeletal muscle, dermis).
Wrong. It forms urogenital organs.

options.t: Visceral (splanchnic) layer of lateral plate mesoderm
options.e: Correct. It gives cardiac muscle, smooth muscle of gut and respiratory organs, and visceral serous layers.

questions.q: Rapid growth of which structures causes the lateral folds of the embryonic disc in the 4th week?

options.e: Correct. Growth of the somites widens the disc and causes lateral folding.
Wrong. CNS growth lengthens the disc and causes the head and tail folds.
Wrong. It induces the neural plate; it is not the cause of folding.
Wrong. The yolk sac is divided by folding; it does not cause it.

questions.q: After folding of the embryonic disc, the amnio-ectodermal junction shifts to the ventral surface of the embryo. What ring does it form?

options.e: Wrong. This is at the cranial end of the foregut.
Correct. The shifted junction forms the primitive umbilical ring, and the connecting stalk becomes the umbilical cord.
Wrong. This is at the caudal end of the hindgut.
Wrong. Not a structure formed by the amnio-ectodermal junction.

questions.q: Which structure extends as a diverticulum from the hindgut into the connecting stalk?

options.e: Wrong. This connects the midgut to the yolk sac.
Wrong. This is the remnant of the allantois, not its origin.
Correct. The allantois is the hindgut diverticulum that enters the connecting stalk.
Wrong. The yolk sac is a separate structure.

questions.q: A 12-year-old boy has painless rectal bleeding. A technetium scan shows ectopic gastric mucosa in an ileal outpouching about 60 cm from the ileocecal valve. Persistence of which embryonic structure causes this?

options.e: Wrong. It extends from the hindgut into the connecting stalk.
Wrong. It becomes the umbilical cord.
Wrong. It lies at the caudal end of the gut.
Correct. Persistence of the middle part of the vitelline duct gives Meckel's diverticulum.

questions.q: At the beginning of the 5th week an embryo shows limb buds. The upper limb buds appear opposite which segments?

options.e: Correct. Upper limbs arise at C4 to T1; lower limbs at lumbar and upper sacral levels.
Wrong. Upper limb buds lie opposite C4 to T1.
Wrong. Upper limb buds lie opposite C4 to T1.
Wrong. The segments are C4 to T1.

questions.q: At the end of the embryonic period (end of the 8th week), the crown-rump (CR) length of the embryo is about:

options.e: Correct. The CR length is used in the 2nd month and reaches about 3 cm at the end of the embryonic period.
Wrong. Too small for the end of week 8.
Wrong. About 3 cm at the end of the embryonic period.
Wrong. This is closer to the fetus at 3 months.
